A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Zero-Flow Encoders with the same authors and research framework. All 24 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–F, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original graphical-model simulations, S&P 500 data analysis, and image-representation experiments, including numerical results in Tables 1–2 and supplementary graphical-model results.

after.justification: v2 retains original graphical-model and financial-data results and reports image experiments on additional datasets, including classification accuracy, reconstruction errors, and reconstruction examples.

M1.justification: The reported amortized objective now places the mask-dependent sparsity penalty inside the expectation over masks (v1 Equation 9; v2 Equation 10). Section 3.3 also revises the sampling description from shuffled data to bootstrap draws with replacement. These are limited revisions to the stated training formulation; the principal zero-flow loss and encoder architectures remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds STL-10, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-1K evaluations and reconstruction as a downstream task. Digit-MNIST disappears, while Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 retain illustrative shortcut experiments but lose their Table 2 classification results. Graphical-model and S&P 500 coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Graphical-model comparisons retain Graphical Lasso and PC with Fisher’s Z tests. Image comparisons retain SimCLR and MAE. Applying these image comparators to the new benchmarks does not introduce a different comparator set.

E3.justification: The added image evaluations introduce reconstruction MSE alongside linear-probe accuracy and specify watermark patches covering one ninth of the image. Section 3.3 revises the stated sampling approximation to bootstrap sampling with replacement. Retained graphical-model protocols and appendix training budgets are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds reconstruction-based diagnosis of shortcut dependence through Table 2 MSE results and ImageNet-1K examples in Figure 7. The existing loss curves and Fashion-MNIST visualization remain. The unseen-target Markov blanket analysis was already in v1 Appendix E.2 and is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random trials for graphical-model recovery, with standard-deviation reporting described in Appendix D, and five-seed mean MAE linear-probing accuracy in Appendix F.3.4. Neither Table 2 provides uncertainty intervals, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the earlier small-dataset accuracy results with new accuracy and reconstruction results. On ImageNet-1K, Zero-Flow, SimCLR, and MAE report 7.01%, 0.10%, and 8.1% accuracy, respectively. MAE leads accuracy on all three new benchmarks; Zero-Flow leads reconstruction MSE on two. These are different-setting results, not performance changes on retained benchmarks. Table 1 is unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects antisymmetry from velocities evaluated at separate interpolated inputs, X_t and X_{1-t}, to the same-location identity v_t(z) = -v_{1-t}(z). The antisymmetry theorem displayed as Theorem 3.2 in v2 already existed as Theorem C.1 in v1; the principal proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and main conclusion retain the zero-flow equivalence, sufficient representation learning, amortized Markov blankets, and shortcut-robustness contributions. Additional experiments support these existing claims. The proposed latent-space extension is explicitly future work.

C2.justification: v2 explains shortcut saturation through SimCLR’s instance-discrimination objective and interprets reconstructions as evidence about information retained beyond the watermark. Section 6.2 uses the more qualified 'less vulnerable' wording and recognizes MAE’s robustness. The existing limitations remain, with a new proposed latent-space route for high-dimensional or discrete targets.

D1.justification: v2 specifies bootstrap sampling with replacement and the one-ninth-area watermark construction for the added datasets. Architecture descriptions, optimizer settings, training budgets, and the code-access link are otherwise retained. Appendix F receives no corresponding detailed account of training the new reconstruction comparisons.

R1.justification: v2 adds dataset references for STL-10, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, ImageNet, and Fashion-MNIST. Research positioning is largely unchanged. The Poole-to-Tian citation change refers to the same 'What makes for good views' paper and is a bibliographic correction.

P1.justification: v2 locally expands the MAE background and shortcut explanation, rewrites Section 6.2, promotes the existing antisymmetry statement and amortization experiment into the main text, and adds acknowledgements and future-work prose. Most of the narrative structure and appendix text remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1 and the Appendix A illustration, moves the lattice blanket visualization into the main text, and adds an ImageNet reconstruction panel. Table 2 changes from dataset columns to dataset-method rows with accuracy and MSE columns. Most other figures retain their content despite relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: Broader image benchmarks and reconstruction diagnostics strengthen the evidence that Zero-Flow retains information beyond watermarks. Clearer illustrations and mathematical corrections also help. The net gain is limited: Table 2 replaces earlier quantitative evaluations, and the largely unchanged Appendix F does not adequately explain training for the new reconstruction comparisons.
